description: A single-panel figure that is a data table rendered as an image (no micrograph, curve or schematic present). The header row reads "Specimens Id", "Ferrite (δ) (MPa)", "Untransformed austenite (MPa)" and "Reverted austenite /Martensite (MPa)", separated from the data by a horizontal rule. Row 1, "Hot rolled & quenched", gives 4439±206, 4080±360 and 8897±550 MPa; row 2, "IA750_5 Min", gives 4267±264, 4351±575 and 3867±110 MPa; row 3, "IA750_60 Min", gives 4150±200, 4196±324 and 3478±334 MPa. Every entry is a mean with a ± standard deviation. The table's argument is that the hot rolled & quenched condition contains by far the hardest "Reverted austenite /Martensite" constituent (8897 MPa, roughly 2.3× the annealed values), whereas intercritical annealing at 750 °C for 5 or 60 min markedly softens that constituent and also lowers δ-ferrite hardness slightly, while untransformed austenite hardness stays nearly constant (4080-4351 MPa). The caption labels these values "Nano hardness" for the HRQ (hot rolled & quenched) and annealed specimens.

observations.observation: The figure consists of a single three-column data table with the header row: "Specimens Id", "Ferrite (δ) (MPa)", "Untransformed austenite (MPa)", "Reverted austenite /Martensite (MPa)".
The table contains exactly three specimen rows: "Hot rolled & quenched", "IA750_5 Min" and "IA750_60 Min".
For "Hot rolled & quenched" the printed values are 4439±206 MPa (Ferrite (δ)), 4080±360 MPa (Untransformed austenite) and 8897±550 MPa (Reverted austenite /Martensite).
For "IA750_5 Min" the printed values are 4267±264 MPa, 4351±575 MPa and 3867±110 MPa for Ferrite (δ), Untransformed austenite and Reverted austenite /Martensite respectively.
For "IA750_60 Min" the printed values are 4150±200 MPa, 4196±324 MPa and 3478±334 MPa for Ferrite (δ), Untransformed austenite and Reverted austenite /Martensite respectively.
Every tabulated entry is a mean followed by a ± standard deviation, and all values carry the unit MPa.
The "Reverted austenite /Martensite" hardness is highest for "Hot rolled & quenched" (8897±550 MPa), about 2.3 times the annealed values (3867±110 and 3478±334 MPa).
Ferrite (δ) hardness decreases monotonically across the listed conditions: 4439 → 4267 → 4150 MPa for "Hot rolled & quenched", "IA750_5 Min" and "IA750_60 Min".
"Untransformed austenite" hardness is nearly constant across all three conditions, lying between 4080 and 4351 MPa.

The caption states that the table reports nano hardness of hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) and annealed specimens; the caption uses the abbreviation HRQ while the table row prints "Hot rolled & quenched".

The caption calls the quantity "Nano hardness" but the table units are printed as MPa, not GPa; the image itself does not state the measurement method (nanoindentation) — that comes only from the caption.
The caption labels the phases/constituents as ferrite (δ), untransformed austenite and reverted austenite/martensite, matching the table column headings.
